## Answer

New services must use **`gateway-api`**. The deciding file is [`policy/ingress-class/v3.yaml`](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra/blob/git-access-ab/r200/policy/ingress-class/v3.yaml) in `dshnayder-org/infra` on branch `git-access-ab/r200` (revision `e7d5fda895e3a9b7de9354d49235088c8fa3e0cc`).

## Evidence

Verbatim from `policy/ingress-class/v3.yaml`:

```
# policy: ingress-class
# version: v3   effective: 2026-04-19   status: current
# subject: which ingress implementation new services must use
apiVersion: policy.meridian.io/v1
kind: FleetPolicy
metadata:
  name: ingress-class-v3
spec:
  effectiveFrom: 2026-04-19
  status: current
  setting: gateway-api
```

## Why this one is authoritative

Three versions of the policy exist and all three carry the same `subject:` line, so they are the same policy over time, not competing rules. Only `v3` is marked current:

| File | `setting` | `status` | `effectiveFrom` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `policy/ingress-class/v1.yaml` | `nginx` | `superseded` | `2024-03-11` |
| `policy/ingress-class/v2.yaml` | `gce-ingress` | `superseded` | `2025-06-02` |
| `policy/ingress-class/v3.yaml` | `gateway-api` | `current` | `2026-04-19` |

- `v1` says `status: superseded` and its header reads `# version: v1   effective: 2024-03-11   status: superseded by v2` — value `nginx`.
- `v2` says `status: superseded` and its header reads `# version: v2   effective: 2025-06-02   status: superseded by v3` — value `gce-ingress`.
- `v3` is the only one with `status: current`, and it is the newest `effectiveFrom`. This matches every other policy family in the repo (`backup-schedule`, `key-rotation`, `log-retention`, `node-image`, `psa-mode`) — in each, exactly `v3` is `current`.

No conflict: `nginx` and `gce-ingress` appear only in the two files that declare themselves superseded.

## Caveats

- There is **no enforcing admission policy** in the repo — no OPA/Gatekeeper constraint, no Kyverno policy, and no `ingressClassName` anywhere. `gateway-api` is a declared fleet standard, not a machine-enforced one.
- An open proposal, [PR #158](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra/pull/158), proposes changing `v3` from `gateway-api` to `envoy-gateway`. It is not merged — the branch content above is unchanged — so `gateway-api` is the answer today. Proposal listing through the version-control broker returned `vcs request failed`, so I could not re-read the PR's current state; treat its status as unverified.

Service account keys are **not used** in this fleet: the current policy is `workload-identity-only`. It is declared in [`policy/key-rotation/v3.yaml`](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra/blob/git-access-ab/r200/policy/key-rotation/v3.yaml), effective `2026-04-19`, and it supersedes the two rotation-based policies that came before it.

## What the repo does not say

- These three files are the **only** statements about service account keys anywhere on the branch. A case-insensitive sweep for `service account key`, `workload identity`, `credential`, `keyfile` and `iam.gserviceaccount` matched nothing else in docs, Terraform (`modules/gke-cluster/variables.tf`), Config Connector manifests or CI.
- So `workload-identity-only` is asserted as a setting with **no prose defining it** — nothing in the repo states whether existing keys must be deleted, how exceptions are granted, or how enforcement is checked. Don't read those in from general GKE practice.
- Loose end worth a look: [`scripts/rotate-keys.sh`](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra/blob/git-access-ab/r200/scripts/rotate-keys.sh) still ships and its header says it is *"Invoked by `.github/workflows/rotate.yml`"* — but it rotates *fleet signing keys*, not SA keys, and that workflow file does not exist on this branch (there is no `.github/` directory at all).

The fleet standardises on **`cos-containerd`** — Container-Optimized OS with the containerd runtime.

## Source

The value is declared in a versioned fleet policy, not in any cluster or node-pool definition:

[`policy/node-image/v3.yaml`](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra/blob/git-access-ab/r200/policy/node-image/v3.yaml) (line 13), on branch `git-access-ab/r200` of [dshnayder-org/infra](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra), revision `e7d5fda895e3a9b7de9354d49235088c8fa3e0cc`:

```yaml
# policy: node-image
# version: v3   effective: 2026-04-19   status: current
# subject: which node image the fleet standardises on
apiVersion: policy.meridian.io/v1
kind: FleetPolicy
metadata:
  name: node-image-v3
spec:
  effectiveFrom: 2026-04-19
  status: current
  setting: cos-containerd
```

## Don't be misled by the older versions

`policy/node-image/` holds three files, and only v3 is current. Both others carry `status: superseded` and are historical:

- `v1.yaml` — `setting: ubuntu-containerd`, effective `2024-03-11`, superseded
- `v2.yaml` — `setting: cos-docker`, effective `2025-06-02`, superseded
- `v3.yaml` — `setting: cos-containerd`, effective `2026-04-19`, **current**

## Nothing else in the repo sets a node image

I searched the whole tree for `image_type`, `imageType`, `cos`, `ubuntu`, `containerd` and `image`. The only matches anywhere are the three policy files above. In particular:

- The 29 cluster directories under `clusters/` define `Cluster` and `NodePool` resources with `machineType`, node counts and `maxSurge` only — no image field. Each inherits fleet policy via a `policy-base.yaml` with `inherit: true`.
- `docs/generated/fleet-inventory.txt` records cluster, region, node count and version — no image.
- `modules/`, `services/`, `scripts/` and `vendor/` contain no node-image reference.

So `cos-containerd` is the single authoritative value, and it applies fleet-wide through policy inheritance rather than being repeated per cluster.

The current backup cadence for production clusters is **`hourly-incremental`**, set by [`policy/backup-schedule/v3.yaml`](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra/blob/git-access-ab/r200/policy/backup-schedule/v3.yaml) on branch `git-access-ab/r200`.

## Verbatim values

`policy/backup-schedule/v3.yaml` — `status: current`, `effectiveFrom: 2026-04-19`:
```
spec:
  effectiveFrom: 2026-04-19
  status: current
  setting: hourly-incremental
```
Its header comment states the subject explicitly: `# subject: the backup cadence for production clusters`.

Two superseded versions exist in the same directory:

| File | `effectiveFrom` | `status` | `setting` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `policy/backup-schedule/v1.yaml` | `2024-03-11` | `superseded` | `nightly-full` |
| `policy/backup-schedule/v2.yaml` | `2025-06-02` | `superseded` | `weekly-full` |

So: `nightly-full` (v1, from `2024-03-11`) → `weekly-full` (v2, from `2025-06-02`) → `hourly-incremental` (v3, current, from `2026-04-19`). Only v3 is current; the other two are marked `superseded` in their own `spec.status`.

## Not present in the repository

- **No cron expression, `schedule:` string, or time-of-day** anywhere. The cadence exists only as the policy keyword `hourly-incremental`.
- **No retention value** for backups. `policy/log-retention/` covers logs, not backups.
- **No GKE `BackupPlan`, `CronJob`, or Helm values file** implements this policy — a `git grep` for backup/schedule/retention/cadence/cron across all 201 tracked files matches nothing outside `policy/backup-schedule/` and the unrelated `policy/log-retention/` files.
- Per-cluster dirs (`clusters/prod-us-central1*/`) carry only `policy-base.yaml` with `inherit: true`, so they take the fleet policy without override. The only runbook, `docs/runbooks/восстановление-кластера.md`, mentions checking a backup but states no cadence.

Audit logs are retained **`400-days`** — the verbatim value of `spec.setting` in the current fleet policy, [`policy/log-retention/v3.yaml`](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra/blob/git-access-ab/r200/policy/log-retention/v3.yaml).

## Superseded versions — do not quote these

Two older versions of the same policy sit beside it, both explicitly marked `status: superseded`:

| File | `setting` | Effective | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

## Scope caveat

There is exactly one retention value per version — the policy does not break retention down by audit log type (admin activity vs. data access) or by environment, and no per-cluster override exists. Searching all `201` tracked files for `retention`, `retain`, `retentionPeriod`, `retention_days`, `log sink`, and `lifecycle` returned only these three files: there is no Terraform log sink, no bucket lifecycle rule, and no Config Connector `LoggingLogBucket` in the repository, so `400-days` is a declared fleet policy rather than an enforced backend setting.

## What is *not* in the repo

- **No `pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce|audit|warn` labels anywhere** — `git grep pod-security.kubernetes.io` returns nothing across all `201` tracked files.

## Answer

The rationale is **not** in the manifest or any doc — it lives only in the commit message that set the value. Commit [`d10fd3d`](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra/commit/d10fd3d016c6af4c0ccbe5ab145257f0f960686c) (`fix(clusters): pin maxSurge to 0`, Meridian Platform, 2026-02-01) states verbatim:

That commit changed `maxSurge: PLACEHOLDER` → `maxSurge: 0`. `INC-2219` is referenced but not present anywhere in the repo, so the underlying incident write-up is out of scope of these sources.

## The value in the repo

## Answer

The repo records a rationale, but only in a commit message — not in the manifest, a comment, an ADR, or any doc.

Per commit [`7095401`](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra/commit/7095401c37840adeadff3e026c889431ad1e2f4d) (2026-02-02, "fix(policy): pin requests.cpu to 480"), verbatim body:

> `raised from 320 for the Black Friday freeze and deliberately never lowered, because the rollback would need a control plane resize; see INC-2404.`

So, in the repo's own words: `480` is not a sized-to-demand number. It was a temporary uplift from `320` for the Black Friday freeze, and a lower value was not restored because reverting it would require a control plane resize. The referenced incident `INC-2404` is external — that string appears nowhere else in the repository, so the underlying reasoning is not verifiable from the repo alone.

## Where the value lives

[`policy/quota/payments.yaml`](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra/blob/git-access-ab/r200/policy/quota/payments.yaml) — the whole file, verbatim:

```yaml
# payments
apiVersion: meridian.io/v1
kind: Setting
spec:
  requests.cpu: 480
```

`480` as a CPU quota appears nowhere else in the tree. That commit changed the line from `requests.cpu: PLACEHOLDER`, and it is an ancestor of the branch head `e7d5fda`, so this is the live value on `git-access-ab/r200`.

## What is absent

- No inline comment, ADR, README, or runbook explaining `480`. The only other rationale-bearing text is the commit body above.
- No `ResourceQuota` manifest, Terraform variable, Config Connector resource, or values file sets a payments CPU quota — this single `Setting` is it.
- `320` and `INC-2404` appear nowhere in the tree (only in that commit message).
- **Caveat:** I could not check pull requests or issues — `vcs.py issue list` and `proposal list` both returned `vcs request failed` on every attempt, while `capabilities` succeeded. If a PR description or issue carries more rationale, it is outside what I could read.

The repo does state the reason — it's in the commit message that set the value, not in the file itself.

## The rationale

Commit [`7b62e82`](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra/commit/7b62e82fcdc8d6274647ca051437b12bfa2780ba) — *"fix(modules): pin default_max_pods_per_node to 110"* (Meridian Platform, `2026-02-03`) — body, verbatim:

> `110 not 256 because the secondary range was sized for /24 per node before the VPC was carved, and re-carving it needs a maintenance window nobody has scheduled; see INC-1873.`

In short: it's an IP-addressing constraint, not a capacity preference. The pod secondary range was allocated assuming a `/24` per node, and raising the limit to `256` would require re-carving the VPC — which needs an unscheduled maintenance window. `INC-1873` is referenced as the context.

`modules/gke-cluster/variables.tf` line `5` (branch `git-access-ab/r200`, HEAD `e7d5fda`):

```
spec:
  default_max_pods_per_node: 110
```

That is the **only** occurrence of the setting in the repository — no tfvars, cluster, or policy file overrides it, and there is no other `110` anywhere in the tree.

## What is not in the repo

- No in-file comment, ADR, README, or design doc explains the value — the commit body is the sole rationale.
- `INC-1873` is referenced but **not** present anywhere in the repository; the incident's own detail lives outside this repo.
- The prior commit `f3a3137` added the variable as `default_max_pods_per_node: PLACEHOLDER`, so `110` was never a carried-over default — it was chosen deliberately in `7b62e82`.

## Answer

`310` is set to be **one second past the upstream load balancer drain timeout** — the only value that stopped a burst of `502`s (gateway errors returned to clients during pod shutdown). The rationale is **not** in the manifest; it is only in the commit that set the value.

Source — commit [`69147ac`](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra/commit/69147ac8b20f1d35281e9fdbbdb9395ef0a7eb31) ("fix(services): pin terminationGracePeriodSeconds to 310", 2026-02-04), message body verbatim:

> `310 is one second past the upstream load balancer drain timeout, which is the only value that stops the 502 burst; see INC-2650.`

## Where the value lives

[`services/identity/deployment.yaml`](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra/blob/git-access-ab/r200/services/identity/deployment.yaml) — the whole file, on branch `git-access-ab/r200` (`e7d5fda`):

```yaml
# deployment
apiVersion: meridian.io/v1
kind: Setting
spec:
  terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 310
```

`git blame` attributes line `5` to `69147ac`; lines `1`–`4` come from [`d00ed82`](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra/commit/d00ed82d3d0ebf909324a5e1e30d812da13e7a01) ("chore(services): add deployment"), which added the file with `terminationGracePeriodSeconds: PLACEHOLDER`.

## What is not in the repo

No arithmetic can be shown, because none of the inputs are committed:

- **No adjacent comment.** The only comment in the file is `# deployment` on line `1`.
- **No `preStop` hook, no probe timings, no `BackendConfig`/drain or LB timeout setting anywhere** — `git grep` for `preStop`, `drain`, `probe`, `backendConfig`, `gracePeriod`, `502`, `timeout` across the branch returns only line `5` above (`docs/generated/fleet-inventory.txt` hits are unrelated cluster-version strings).
- **No ADR or runbook covering it.** `docs/runbooks/` contains a single file, `восстановление-кластера.md` (control-plane recovery); there is no ADR directory. `INC-2650` appears nowhere in the tree.
- **`services/` contains only `identity/`,** and `deployment.yaml` is its only file — there is no chart or values file overriding this.

**Labelled inference (not stated in the repo):** the commit message implies the upstream LB drain timeout is `300s` and `310 = 300 + 1s margin`, but no committed file states `300`, so the drain timeout must be confirmed against the load balancer config or `INC-2650`, neither of which is in this repo.

## Answer

`reconcileNodePool` is defined **twice** in [dshnayder-org/infra](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra) on branch `git-access-ab/r200` (tip `e7d5fda895e3a9b7de9354d49235088c8fa3e0cc`). **Which copy the controller compiles cannot be established from this repository** — it contains no Go build system. The only statement on the subject is a source comment, not build evidence.

## The two definitions

Identical signatures, different packages:

- `modules/controller/nodepool.go:5` — package `controller`
  `func reconcileNodePool(ctx context.Context, pool *Pool) error {`
- `vendor/upstream-operator/nodepool.go:5` — package `upstream`
  `func reconcileNodePool(ctx context.Context, pool *Pool) error {`

Their bodies differ only in a label: `return reconcile(ctx, pool, "first-party")` vs `return reconcile(ctx, pool, "vendored")`.

## Why the build question is inconclusive

Verified across the whole branch **and all history** (`git rev-list --all`):

- **No `go.mod`, `go.sum`, `go.work`** — anywhere, ever. Without a module there is no import path, no `vendor/` semantics, and no `replace` directive to inspect.
- **No `package main` and no `func main`** — there is no controller entrypoint in this repo, so there is no import graph to trace.
- **No build constraints** — zero `//go:build` or `// +build` lines in any file.
- **No imports at all** — no `import` statement in any of the four `.go` files, so nothing imports either package; `context.Context` and `Pool` are also undefined here, meaning neither file compiles as it stands.
- **No `vendor/modules.txt`**, no `Makefile`, `Dockerfile`, CI config, or Bazel files.
- The repo holds only 4 Go files (7 lines each): `modules/controller/{nodepool,quota}.go` and `vendor/upstream-operator/{nodepool,quota}.go`.

## The only claim in the repo

`vendor/upstream-operator/nodepool.go:3-4` asserts its own exclusion:

```
// reconcileNodePool is vendored from upstream-operator v0.14.2. Do not edit;
// this copy is not compiled into the controller.
```

and `modules/controller/nodepool.go:3-4` says:

```
// reconcileNodePool is the first-party implementation. It reads the fleet
// policy and reconciles one node pool at a time.
```

That is an author's comment. Taken at face value the first-party copy is the live one, but nothing in the tree — no module, entrypoint, build tag, or exclusion — proves it. Both files entered in one commit, `e364197 chore(fleet): import the Meridian fleet repository`, and neither has been touched since.

If you need this settled, point me at the repo that actually builds the controller binary.

## Answer: the repo does not contain a `prod-atlantis` cluster

There is **no** cluster named `prod-atlantis` anywhere in [dshnayder-org/infra](https://github.com/dshnayder-org/infra) on branch `git-access-ab/r200` (revision `e7d5fda895e3a9b7de9354d49235088c8fa3e0cc`), so no release channel can be quoted for it. I am not guessing a value.

## What I searched

- Case-insensitive search for `atlantis` across all 201 tracked files: **0 matches**. Also 0 matches searching every commit's blobs and `git log -S"atlantis"` across the full history (10 commits, complete history in the bundle). The branch is the only one on the remote.
- Case-insensitive search for `release[_-]?channel`: **28 matches**, all at line `10` of `clusters/<name>/cluster.yaml`, and every one of those 28 clusters is named `prod-us-central1` or `prod-us-central1-2` … `prod-us-central1-28`.
- Also checked `modules/gke-cluster/variables.tf` (Terraform), `policy/`, and `docs/generated/fleet-inventory.txt` (9001 lines, every entry named `meridian-NNNNN`) — no `atlantis` alias or mapping.
